description:
fz-5xp.18 found ONE semantic question -- ordering -- implemented three times, and
the count was the bug. Equality agreed across doors because interp and native
both call fz_value_eq_ref. Ordering disagreed because each door hand-rolled it,
and guards hand-rolled it a third time. `2 >= 1.0` was false on the JIT and true
on interp; `when a >= b` with a = 2, b = 1.0 fell through on BOTH doors.

Nothing tells us ordering was the only one. This epic is about to add a lot of
semantic predicates (String comparison and casing, Map key identity and
ordering, Keyword lookup, Collectable, term ordering itself), and each is a
chance to create a new divergence pair.

WORK: audit the semantic questions that more than one door answers, and for each
say whether there is a single shared implementation or several. Candidates to
start from, each of which has at least one per-door site today:

  truthiness            fz_truthy_ref vs interp's is_truthy
  equality              fz_value_eq_ref (shared) + lower_eq_binop fast paths
                        + interp_value_eq fast paths + Region::Equal in two
                        dispatch lowerings
  ordering              cmp_any_value (shared as of fz-5xp.18) + both-int fast
                        paths + guard_cmp
  arithmetic            fz_op_*_ii/if/fi/ff intrinsics + lower_arith_binop +
                        ir_interp/binop.rs
  runtime type tests    runtime_type_predicate.rs claims ONE table with three
                        lowerings that must each be taught -- verify that claim
                        holds, since it is the design we want everywhere
  bitstring matching    receive.rs emit_bitstring_test vs jobs/native.rs
                        (fz-5xp.1 -- currently one implementation and one hole)
  map key identity      heap/key_cmp.rs vs anything the compiler folds

DELIVERABLE: a short .agent/docs note listing each question, its single owner,
and the per-door fast paths that are allowed to exist beside it. A fast path is
legitimate -- quicksort's zero-scalar-box pin depends on an inline both-int
compare -- but it must be a fast path over shared semantics, not a second
answer.

SIGNAL: for anything found with more than one answer, a fixture comparing the
doors on the cases where they could differ. Note that mixed int/float
comparison survived for as long as it did because NO fixture compared an
integer against a float.
title: Audit: which semantic questions are answered more than once across the doors
